strengths.I006: Improves the ideas themselves at the development stage by making every non-passing claim be repaired against a re-executed check or struck, and it keeps those checks as templates across runs. A lone agent has neither the execution feedback nor prior runs to draw on. The outcome, the falsified-claim rate under a held-out checker from another model family, is measured rather than a matter of rater opinion.
strengths.I003: A cheap, precisely specified change to the scoring module (bootstrap BT with cluster-correlated shifts, then greedy expected-maximum selection). It can be tested offline by replaying saved pairwise records behind an on/off flag, at the cost of one labelling call per brief, and it does not touch card text, so it cannot exploit length or polish bias.

verdicts.reason: I003 only reorders finalists that already exist, so its ceiling is set by their quality. It admits it loses by construction if the benchmark scores the mean of the top 3, and it may give a null result if the finalists are already diverse. I006 raises the substance of the delivered ideas by removing claims that fail a check, which is a gain raters without LLM-judge biases should also prefer.

strengths.I007: It turns the benchmark's own blinded verdicts into a correction to selection. The regularised residual reduces to today's ranking when labels are few, and the nuisance covariates (length, hedges, judge-family match) are fitted and then set to zero. It is cheap (about 4 days, no extra run cost) and can be evaluated cleanly by leave-one-brief-out AUC.
strengths.I006: Execution-grounded repair of the developed ideas, where claims must pass a re-run check or be struck. It compounds across runs through a library of check templates, and its falsified-claim rate is an outcome-level measure that holds up without LLM-judge biases.

verdicts.reason: I007 learns to predict what beats the baseline under the benchmark panel. It needs at least 15 labelled briefs before it switches on, and it risks Goodhart overfitting to the raters. I006 makes the delivered ideas more likely to be correct on any brief with checkable claims, so its benefit extends beyond the benchmark.
